newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-TOP CONTENDERS IN PGA CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-TOP CONTENDERS IN PGA CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: Brief look at some of the top contenders at the PGA Championsip starting on Thursday at Winged Foot Golf Club:

-- Mark Brooks (U.S.) - The defending champion admits he has struggled with his game since winning his first major title at last year's PGA in a one-hole playoff at Valhalla Golf Club. His best finish so far this year was joint seventh at the Players Championship in March.
Number of PGA Championships played: nine
Other notable achievements: winner of seven events on U.S. PGA Tour in 15 years

-- Tiger Woods (U.S.) - Playing in his first PGA Championship after turning pro less than a year ago; looking to add the PGA to his runaway Masters victory in April, when he became youngest Masters winner
Other notable achievements: Winner of record three consecutive U.S. Amateur championships; besides Masters, winner of five other U.S. tour events, including three this year
-- Ernie Els (South Africa) - Has already won two U.S. Opens, including this year's -- and this PGA Championship is being played on a classic "Open" course.

Other notable achievements: Winner of three other U.S. tour events and six in Europe; followed his Open victory in June with another win the next week at the Westchester Classic, played just a few miles from Winged Foot on a similar course.

-- Justin Leonard (U.S.) - Another of golf's "twenty something" rising stars; the newly crowned British Open champion has played well in his only two PGA Championships, tying for fifth last year and eighth the year before
Best finish: joint fifth last year
Other notable achievements: Winner of this year's British Open and joint seventh in the Masters
-- Nick Faldo (Britain) - Would love to add PGA crown to his three Masters and three British Open titles, although his swing has been giving him problems recently.
Other notable achievements: In addition to his six majors, winner of 30 other tour events (three U.S. and 27 European), including this year's Nissan Open

-- Greg Norman (Australia) - Has finished second in two PGA Championships, including a sudden-death playoff loss in 1993; also lost to Fuzzy Zoeller in an 18-hole playoff at a memorable U.S. Open at Winged Foot in 1984
Other notable achievements: winner of two British Opens and 77 other events around the world, including the St. Jude Classic in July
-- Tom Lehman (U.S.) - A veteran of many years on minitours, he has one of the best records in recent majors, topped by his victory in last year's British Open.
Other notable achievements: Leading money winner on U.S. tour last year, when he also had lowest score average; member of 1995 Ryder Cup team

-- Jose Maria Olazabal (Spain) - Having returned from 18 months of inactivity due to injury, he is trying to play his way onto Europe's Ryder Cup team and a good showing in the PGA would help solidify a spot for him
Other notable achievements: Winner of the 1994 Masters and 19 other tour events; a stalwart on Ryder Cup teams since 1987
-- Colin Montgomerie (Britain) - Leading money winner on the European tour the past four years, the big Briton lost sudden- death playoff in 1995 PGA Championship.
Other notable achievements: Winner of 13 European tour events, including two this year; second in this year's U.S. Open after losing a playoff in '94 Open
-- Jesper Parnevik (Sweden) - Sweden's most successful male golfer now plays full-time on American tour, where he has four second-place finishes
Best finish: joint fifth last year
Other notable achievements: Six international victories, including three on European tour; runnerup in 1997 and 1994 British Opens
-- Phil Mickelson (U.S.) - This former college golf star has three top-10 finishes in four PGA Championships and his game is well-suited for Winged Foot.

Other notable achievements: first golfer since Jack Nicklaus to win 10 U.S. tour events by the age of 26; won four times last year and twice this year, including the Sprint International two weeks ago. REUTER
